title: Independence of Cartan--Eilenberg comparison maps on the derived spectral sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathcal A$. Choose injective resolutions $X\to J_X^\bullet$ and $Y\to J_Y^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and Cartan--Eilenberg injective resolutions of $F(J_X^\bullet)$ and $F(J_Y^\bullet)$ as supplied by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. Any two choices of comparison maps lifting $f$ give the same maps, from the second page onward, between the spectral sequences of the filtration by the Cartan--Eilenberg resolution degree on the total complexes after applying $G$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. These maps compose as the maps induced by $f$ compose, and the isomorphisms of the second pages with $R^pG(R^qF(-))$ and of the abutments with $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}G(I))$ commute with them.

proof.text: Choose injective resolutions of $X$ and $Y$ and Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions of their $F$-images as in [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. That node indexes $I^{p,q}$ with columns $I^{p,\bullet}$ resolving $K^p$, so $p$ is the complex degree and $q$ the resolution degree. [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-eilenberg-functorial] uses the exchanged convention $C^{p,q}=I^{q,p}$ (rows $C^{\bullet,q}$ resolve $K^q$, augmentation into $C^{0,\bullet}$); under this exchange its clauses (1)--(6) are exactly the properties supplied by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists], and its first degree is the resolution degree here, while the second-degree filtration in its conclusion is the complex-degree filtration, which is not the one used here. A comparison lift of $f$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-eilenberg-functorial] with the identity exact functor on $\mathcal B$ and $u=F(\beta)$ for a lift $\beta:J_X^\bullet\to J_Y^\bullet$ of $f$. Being a morphism of double complexes, it preserves bidegrees, so after applying the additive functor $G$ its total map preserves the resolution-degree filtration ${}''F$ of [def-sp-double-complex-total] (in the indexing $I^{p,q}$); thus it is a filtered chain map.

If two comparison lifts are chosen, their underlying lifts $\beta,\beta':J_X^\bullet\to J_Y^\bullet$ of $f$ may differ. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] with $\alpha$ the quasi-isomorphism from $X$ (in degree $0$) to $J_X^\bullet$ gives a homotopy $k$ between $\beta$ and $\beta'$, so $F(k)$ is a homotopy between $u=F(\beta)$ and $u'=F(\beta')$, $F$ being additive. Apply [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-comparison-homotopy] to the identity exact functor on $\mathcal B$, the complexes $F(J_X^\bullet)$ and $F(J_Y^\bullet)$ (zero in negative degrees), their Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions from [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists], and the homotopic maps $u,u'$. The resulting total homotopy $H$ lowers the resolution-degree filtration by one; since $G$ is additive, $G(H)$ is a homotopy between the two total maps after applying $G$ with the same one-step filtration shift.

The Cartan--Eilenberg double complexes are first-quadrant, so the resolution-degree filtrations on their total complexes are bounded in each total degree. Apply [lem-sp-filtered-homotopy-spectral-sequence] with its one-step filtration shift to the homotopy from Step 2. Their maps on every page $E_r$ for $r\ge2$ coincide, as do the maps on the abutment filtration and its graded pieces [def-sp-convergence]. Thus the comparison maps are independent of all choices from the second page onward.

source.place: functoriality and homotopy invariance of the spectral sequence of a filtered complex

proof.text: Choose the identity lift for an identity map and compare any other lift with it by Steps 2--3; this makes the induced page maps identities. For composable maps, choose comparison lifts whose middle Cartan--Eilenberg resolution is shared. Their composite satisfies the augmentation equation for the composite map, so it can be compared by Steps 2--3 with any independently chosen lift of that composite; [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] handles the possible difference in the underlying injective-resolution lift. Functoriality of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] then identifies the induced page maps with those of the corresponding complex maps. Its first-page and abutment formulas for the second filtration, together with the Cartan--Eilenberg resolution properties in [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists] (the horizontal cycles and boundaries in each resolution degree are injective), [lem-sp-cart-eilenberg-left-exact-cohomology] (so $H^p_I(G(I^{\bullet,q}))\cong G(H^p_I(I^{\bullet,q}))$ on the first page, naturally in the comparison maps), and the derived-functor computation in [def-sp-left-exact-additive], identify the second page with $R^pG(R^qF(-))$ and the abutment with $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}G(I))$; these identifications are induced by the same filtered maps and hence commute with them.
